composition.story: How does gradient descent reduce error? Start with a model setting on a positive slope, then move opposite that slope. Compare the error before and after. Here, error is w², and each update subtracts half the slope. This chosen step reaches the minimum; other problems usually require repeated updates.

aha.observation: Moving opposite the slope lowers error, as the before-and-after comparison shows.

Use the canonical algorithm/collection arrangement with two named regions on one row. Highlight only the active region; do not animate movement.
Give each measurement one location. The model setting is dimensionless; error uses squared setting units. Values are exact, without rounding. Arrows compare before with after.
Anchor the text to the active region without covering labels. Render the reason as the bound status line below the experiment.
